## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit_clip.rs` and `edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

</system-reminder>

content.content:
---
# 1. What this is

A screencast editor without a recorder — and, since road map 3,
a recorder of the SCREEN, and since §11 CAM-1 of a camera beside it or on its
own, whose output is ordinary media. Open one or
more video files from disk, arrange them on layered tracks over a fixed canvas, trim,
split, annotate, animate, and export. Mac only, Apple Silicon, macOS 26+.

The bar is a balance: enough to make a real cut with text,
shapes, transitions and simple animation, without Final Cut's magnetic
timeline, roles, multicam, scopes, or a plugin ecosystem.

Deliberate non-goals: multicam, color grading beyond
per-clip controls (§11 GR-1: tier 1 of grading — tone, adjustment clips,
looks, LUT import, an ungraded switch and one luma waveform — is in, kept by
the owner's verdict of 2026-10-10, and tier 2's scopes, colour wheels,
curves and qualifiers beside it, GR-10…GR-13; tier 3's HDR→SDR conversion
and camera log are in, GR-15, GR-16; the HDR road map's HLG timeline, its
HLG, HDR10 and SDR-version deliverables, HDR scopes, the PQ peak, Canon Log
2 and 3 and opt-in linear-light blending are in, HD-1…HD-17; a wide-gamut
working space for SDR projects is not wanted, GR-20; tier 4's vectorscope zoom,
hue curves, the blend between curves of different point counts and the
qualifier's cleanup blur are in, GR-24, GR-31…GR-35, while an Offset
wheel, a qualifier on picture clips, 1,024-level scopes and a histogram
behind the curves are not wanted, GR-27…GR-30), a plugin system (a clip may
draw itself from a JavaScript module in its package, road map 10; nothing
else is scriptable — §11 G-1),
motion blur, stabilisation, optical-flow retiming and auto-reframe (heavy
pixel work or ML, outside the compositor's one-pass shape — road map 2 §4),
any platform but macOS. **Screen recording was on this list until road map 3
reversed it** (§11): the app records a display or a window through
ScreenCaptureKit into a file it then imports exactly as File ▸ Open would —
paused and resumed from the menu bar, each stretch its own file and its own
clip; callouts reconstructed after the fact stay out. **Camera recording
was on it too until §11 CAM-1** (road map "camera-recording") reversed it: a
camera alone or beside a screen recording, each its own file and clip.
**Audio beyond what shipped was on it too until §11 AU-2** (road map
"audio", 2026-10-30) lifted it: EQ, track and bus processing, and Apple's
built-in audio units are in, beside Frame Job's own DSP; hosting
third-party Audio Unit plug-ins stays out, under the plugin system above.

**The opening flow is the point.** File > Open on a `.mov` or `.mp4` (or a
drop on the Dock icon, or the welcome window's Open Video…) creates an
*untitled* project sized to that file, with the file as the first clip on
Track 1, ready to cut. Save then writes a `.framejob` package next to the
source. The app is also the Alternate handler for movie, audio and image
types so Open With… works from the Finder.

content.content:
Scaling, rotating and cropping do not snap (⇧ while rotating snaps the angle
to 15° steps instead). A guide line is drawn across the canvas on each axis that snapped. Press
**N** or choose **View ▸ Snapping** to turn snapping on or off. The timeline
uses the same setting. Hold ⌘ during a drag to stop snapping for that drag.

### Safe areas

**View ▸ Safe Areas**, or the toolbar's **Safe** checkbox, draws two guide
frames over the canvas, at 90 % and 80 % of its size. They are guides only
and never appear in an export. The app remembers the setting.

### Editing an action's end state on the canvas

With an action selected on the clip's action lane, a move, scale, rotate or
crop drag, or an arrow-key nudge, edits that action's end state, just as the
inspector's fields do. The box on screen still shows the frame at the
playhead. There are two exceptions: a drag on a multi-clip selection, and a
shape's box resize, both edit the clip itself. See
[Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md).

## Crop

Press **C**, or double-click a clip that is not text, to enter crop mode for
the selected clip. The eight handles become crop edges, and the part being
cut away is shown as a dim ghost inside the uncropped frame. Press **Esc** or
**Return**, or click empty canvas, to leave crop mode.

content.content:
### Loudness

Loudness normalises the whole mix to an integrated loudness target, measured to ITU-R BS.1770-4.

| Choice | Target |
|---|---|
| **Off** | No normalisation. The export still measures its sound and reports it. |
| **−14 LUFS (streaming)** | Where the main streaming services normalise. |
| **−16 LUFS** | The usual target for stereo podcasts. |
| **−23 LUFS (broadcast)** | EBU R 128 broadcast delivery. |
| **Custom…** | Type any target from −70 to 0 LUFS, to one decimal place. |

How normalisation works:

- The export measures the real mix first. The progress line reads "Measuring loudness…" during this pass.
- It then applies **one gain** to everything. Levels inside the timeline keep their relationship to each other.
- The gain is worked out through the export's master limiter (below), so the file lands on the target even when its loudest peaks would pass the ceiling: those peaks are turned down instead of the whole mix. Only a target more than 40 dB above the mix falls short.

**Every export with sound goes through a master limiter**, normalised or not. It keeps the file's true peak under **−1 dBTP**: a mix that would pass that, from loud clips, a crossfade between two loud clips, a nest turned up or an action that raises a clip's volume, is limited instead of clipped. Sound under the ceiling passes through untouched, sample for sample. The limiter looks 3.3 ms ahead, and the export takes that back, so the sound stays exactly in sync with the picture. The preview has no master limiter: what you hear while editing is the mix before it.

A track's own compressor and limiter ([Audio](audio.md#track-compressor-and-limiter)) run before the master, on that track's sound alone, exactly as set: the export plays each such track on its own through them and mixes the tracks afterwards. The measurement for a loudness target hears them too, so the file still lands on the target. The master is only the loudness gain and this limiter; there is no master compressor or EQ. To compress the whole mix, nest everything onto one track and give that track a compressor.

The sheet fixes the ceiling at −1 dBTP. An agent can choose another (see [For agents](#for-agents)). Loudness is greyed out for GIF and APNG.

For per-clip levels, fades and Normalize, see [Audio](audio.md).

### Range
245:**File ▸ Save Frame…** (⌥⌘E) saves the frame under the playhead as a still. The save panel suggests the project's name and the timecode, with `-` for `:` (`Board 00-00-12-05.png`). Its **Format** popup offers:
265:Save Frame… is greyed out while the timeline is empty.
341:- `render_frame` renders one frame through the same path as Save Frame…. It returns the image inline and as a file, and with no `path` it writes a temporary PNG and names it. An explicit `format` wins and replaces the path's extension, so `{path: "shot.jpg", format: "png"}` writes `shot.png`. When a graphic in the frame warned or failed, the reply names it, its frame and the message, and a failed graphic draws its error card in the picture. It takes `t` (default: the playhead), `path`, `format` (`png`, `jpeg`, `heic`), `max_width` and `burn_in_timecode`, plus `sdr_version`, `ungraded`, `selection` and the scope measurements described in [Colour grading](color-grading.md) and [HDR and colour](hdr-and-color.md).

Final Cut Pro 12 added Visual Search alongside Transcript Search, and reviewers are split on how well they work.

**What it is:** Visual Search lets you find moments by what appears on screen. Apple's own Final Cut Pro 12 guide describes it as a way to locate moments, objects, and actions using natural language (Final Cut Pro 12 introduces Transcript Search (which allows you to find spoken words or phrases in footage) and Visual Search (which enables you to locate moments, objects, and actions) using natural language (both require a Mac with Apple silicon).). Analysis runs in the background, and by default, when you import media containing dialog, FCP automatically analyzes it.

**Positive reviews:** ProVideo Coalition's reviewer called Visual Search well integrated and a very useful addition to the app. Another piece noted that speed has always been one of the hallmarks of Final Cut, and Visual Search supports that.

**Criticism:** Larry Jordan was harsh. In one test, a search for horses found 30 clips – 7 with one or more horses and 23 without any horses at all! He concluded that the way both Transcript search and Visual search are implemented make them highly limited and unreliable. In another comparison, Final Cut Pro's visual search didn't find all the instances of "wheelchair" that the other two did.

**Limitations:** Compound clips are excluded. Apple's guidance says compound clips aren't analyzed and don't appear in Transcript or Visual search results. Multicam and synced clips are also not analyzed directly, though their source clips can appear in results.

Sources conflict mainly on reliability. Reviewers who praise the feature focus on speed and integration, while Jordan's testing found frequent misses and false positives.

A ProVideo Coalition tutorial adds that partial sentences work and can come from anywhere in the transcript. It opens as a new timeline, named after your clip with "- Paper Edit" on the end.
- **Sources:** Paper Edit works on raw clips and existing sequences, according to the same tutorial. Adobe's community announcement describes it as a way to assemble rough cuts directly from your transcript.
- **Limitations (from user feedback in Adobe's beta forum):** Users reported that you can't cut or copy inside Paper Edit mode, and that ranged markers can't be set there. Requests included duplicate-take detection and search within Paper Edit. Those comments came from the June 2026 beta, so 26.5 may differ.

Media Intelligence is Premiere Pro's AI search feature for finding clips by describing them in plain language. The sources are mostly from the 2024–2025 launch period, and their accounts of its release status differ.

- **How it works:** The feature builds a semantic index of your footage using an on-device machine learning model, rather than relying on manually tagged keywords. The index is stored either in the project's media cache or as sidecar files (.prmi). Analysis runs locally; Adobe says it does not see or train on your footage or searches, and all analysis and search happen locally on your computer without using the internet.
- **Searching:** You open the Search panel from the magnifying glass in the upper right corner. Descriptive phrases work, such as "drone shot of a mountain at sunrise." One source notes that visual search can give better results the more specific you are in describing the scene.
- **Other search types:** Transcript and metadata searches work differently. The Search panel uses exact text matches for transcripts and metadata and natural language descriptions for visuals. Metadata such as the camera used, the focal length used or the date of recording can also be used as filters.
- **Language limits:** At the beta stage, one report said the natural language search was currently English only. A forum user reported that a Russian query returned no results, which suggests limited non-English support at that time.
- **Release status:** Sources disagree. One describes Media Intelligence as new with Premiere Pro 2025, while an earlier beta announcement described it as now in beta. A German report says the search function is now part of the full version.
- **Performance and control:** Analysis runs in the background, and Premiere Pro will prioritize playback over the background analysis. You can turn it off in Preferences > Media Analysis & Transcription. If you share a project, it's best to include the .prin file.

I ran one search, so these points come from secondary articles and community posts. For current language support and release status, check Adobe's official Media Intelligence FAQ.

Gling is an AI editor for talking-head video that removes silences, filler words, and bad takes, and it has a free tier. The sources disagree on paid pricing, so check the official site before relying on any figure.

**What it does:** Gling automatically detects and cuts silences, filler words, and repeated or bad takes. **Caveats:** Most of these sources are affiliate-style review or SEO pages, and one listing says Gling is subscription with a trial/free option; check current pricing. Treat the prices above as unverified until confirmed on gling.ai.

I ran one search. None of the results cite an official YouTube safe-zone spec, and the third-party figures don't agree with each other.

**TikTok:** The most consistent figures come from a tool that works from TikTok's own published ad template. On a 1080×1920 frame, it advises keeping text, faces and logos out of the top 240 px, the bottom 660 px, and 120 px on each side ([Socialync](https://www.socialync.io/tools/safe-zones/tiktok)). Upload-Post reports the same margins, plus a button column on the right from 840 px down ([Upload-Post](https://www.upload-post.com/tools/safe-zone-checker/)). The two disagree on that column's width: Socialync puts it at 180 px, Upload-Post at 300 px. Those numbers come from TikTok's ad template, so they may not match organic posts. Other guides give quite different values. One lists a 900×1492 central area with a 320 px bottom dead zone ([PostPlanify](https://postplanify.com/blog/social-media-safe-zones-2026-complete-guide)), and that page's own figures also shift between sections.

**YouTube Shorts:** Revid describes the Shorts safe zone as an 840×960 px area on a 1080×1920 canvas, starting 288 px from the top and 48 px from the left ([Revid](https://www.revid.ai/youtube-shorts-safe-zone)). Poster.ly instead says to keep critical content in the central 50% vertically for ads, because the CTA button adds bottom UI ([Poster.ly](https://www.poster.ly/tools/youtube-shorts-safe-zone-checker)). A third set of figures, a 984×1500 central area with a 120 px top dead zone, comes from a PostPlanify-derived guide ([Adaptly](https://adaptlypost.com/fr/blog/social-media-safe-zones-2026-complete-guide)).

**Bottom line:** For TikTok, the 240/660/120 px margins on a 1080×1920 frame are the best-sourced numbers, since they trace back to TikTok's own ad template. For YouTube Shorts, no result gives a verified official value, so the 840×960 box at (48, 288) is the most specific candidate but is unconfirmed. Previewing the upload in the app is the safest check, since the interface changes often.

115:**The transcript cache.** Each media file's transcript is kept in the project package and reused by the next run. A file whose cached transcript matches the request (same file, model, language, Speakers and Vocabulary) is not uploaded again and costs nothing. The caption style does not count, so restyling never uploads. A transcript made for Remove Filler Words also serves Generate Captions, so that file is not uploaded or billed again. The cache is kept per media entry, so two media entries over the same file are uploaded and billed separately. When no API key is set and every file in the run already has a current transcript, the hint changes to "Current cached transcripts will be used without an API key or network request." and **Generate** works without a key. With a key set, the usual hint stays, and the summary says there is nothing to upload. To force a fresh upload anyway, tick **Transcribe again**.
127:**Speakers.** With **Speakers** ticked, a change of speaker always starts a new cue or page. In the **Subtitles** style, each speaker's cues take their own colour, in the order the speakers first appear: white, yellow, cyan, green, then round again. Speakers are counted separately for each media file.
147:*Agents:* `transcribe`. It takes `clips` (the scope), `engine` (`apple`, the default, or `assemblyai`), `language` (`auto` by default with AssemblyAI), `style`, `replace`, `slide`, `fill`, `dim`, and, for AssemblyAI only, `speakers`, `vocabulary` and `refresh`, each refused by name without `engine: "assemblyai"`. It answers the cues in timeline ticks (with each word's timing for a word style) whether or not it places them, and `place: false` changes nothing at all. `replace` is refused with `subtitles` or with `place: false`; when it is given, a placed run lists the removed tracks' ids under `replaced`. The tool never remembers the sheet's engine, style or looks, and never downloads a language model. A language whose model is not installed is refused by name.

verdicts.closest_existing: Clip ▸ Remove Silences… and Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words… (sheet, timeline wash, one ripple_delete_ranges undo step; detect_silence/detect_fillers MCP tools), plus get_transcript + ripple_delete_ranges driven by the Assistant for false starts (TR-5). There is no transcript view, no click-a-word-to-seek, no select-and-delete in text, no restore, and no retake detector.
verdicts.feasibility: Feasible, and it reuses existing parts. Word timings are cached per media in MEDIA source ticks (DeviceTranscriptCache.swift: cache/device-transcripts/<media>-<lang>.json; AssemblyAI in cache/transcripts/). MediaTranscript.words(for:in:) and TranscriptReader map them onto a clip in project ticks. rc_project_source_map (ffi_query.rs:146, SR-20) maps through speed, ramps and reverse. ripple_delete_ranges (op_table.rs:273) merges many ranges into ONE undo step and is an MCP tool. FillerDetector already holds the lock, nest and transition protection rules, so a text cut can reuse them. Gaps: (1) Restore is not one existing op. add_clip, insert_clip and overwrite_clip take only track, media and at, so restoring a cut word means insert_time + trim_end into the left clip's handle as one grouped step, and insert_time also shifts every other unlocked track. (2) A whole-timeline view needs the on-device recogniser over every clip, at 'a few seconds per minute of speech', before it fills. Cached per media after that. (3) Fillers in the view are cloud-only: TR-7 measured that the on-device engine kept 1 of 8 fillers. Without an AssemblyAI key the view shows no fillers. (4) MAX_CLIPS = 4096 counts nested clips too (format.rs check_caps). Each text cut splits EVERY unlocked track, so about 1,000 cuts over a 4-track timeline reaches the cap. CONFLICT with spec §11: TR-3 says 'a false start is never offered without a conversation', and AI-6/W-9 say 'no PIPELINE picks words to cut by meaning'. A deterministic retake/false-start pass that strikes words for review is such a pipeline, so it needs a new §11 decision amending TR-3 before code. Fillers and long pauses are fine under TR-3/TR-4. No format change is needed, because cut words are derivable as media words lying between consecutive windows of the same media.
verdicts.platform_apis: Speech SpeechTranscriber (macOS 26.0+, Apple doc JSON) for the on-device transcript; AssemblyAI (BYO key, existing) for fillers and speaker labels; AVPlayer periodic time observer for the word highlight. No new framework needed.
verdicts.market_refutation_attempt: Tried commoditisation: edit-by-transcript is everywhere. verdicts.closest_existing: Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio (move_clip + drift-correcting set_speed as one undo step); per-media Silero speech spans (media_speech.rs, format 29) read per clip by Duck by Speech (audio_duck_speech.rs); the Channels section (AU-34: left/right/both/swapped of a two-channel track); set_enabled. verdicts.feasibility: Feasible as a planner over cached data. Confirmed: CompositionBuilder.firstTrack (CompositionBuilder.swift:423) returns tracks(withMediaType:).first, and it is used for audio by the builder, Silence, the isolation, ramp, voice and reverse renderers and the transcription extract. container.rs indexes only the first video and first audio track. So OBS multi-track files lose tracks 2+. Fixing this means an audio-track index on the media or clip (format bump) and touches every firstTrack(.audio) caller, not just the builder. Confirmed: the 8-decoder budget only WARNS (plan.rs warnings_for). Helpful finding: a clip with enabled.video off is NOT decoded, because nest.rs shows_video gates evaluate.rs:454/477 and the recipe. So stacked angles disabled by set_enabled cost one decode at a time, except in transition overlaps. One undo step does NOT need a new core op: Synchronize Audio already applies an op list as one step. A core op (split + set_enabled across tracks) is wanted for MCP parity and because a 2-hour episode emits thousands of ops. Clip cap: 2 h at one cut per ~8 s is ~900 cuts. Splitting all 3 angle tracks gives ~2,700 clips. If each angle carries a linked sound half (AU-90) that is split with it, ~5,400 is OVER MAX_CLIPS 4096. So the design must cut picture only, keep the mics whole, or use a single program track. Spec §1 lists multicam as a deliberate non-goal (confirmed), so a §11 decision lifting it is needed first. Inputs exist: Silero spans per media through Core ML (SileroVAD.swift), the 10 ms loudness cache, Match Audio and Enhance Voice. AssemblyAI speaker labels exist for captions (BYO key) as an optional diarisation source.

verdicts.market_refutation_attempt: Tried 'already commoditised'. Descript ships Automatic Multicam with active-speaker mode (help.descript.com). Tried 'niche': in-person multi-camera podcasters are a subset of creators. Evidence that survives: YouTube still reports over 1 billion monthly podcast users, from Feb 2025 and repeated May 2026, with TV viewing of podcasts up from 400M to 700M hours a year. verdicts.market_refutation_attempt: Tried commoditisation, and the distinctive half fails. verdicts.closest_existing: Media tab rows with thumbnails, dragged whole onto a track (plain drop, ⌥ insert, ⇧⌥ overwrite), then trimmed or slipped on the timeline; View ▸ Preview Quality Full/Half/Quarter (render size only, not decode). No skimming (MediaRowView hover only paints a fill), no source viewer, no In/Out or favourite ranges on media, no proxies. add_clip, insert_clip and overwrite_clip take only track, media and at.
verdicts.feasibility: Source ranges are an op-table change: add_clip, insert_clip and overwrite_clip gain an optional source in and duration, held inside the file by source_window.rs's one bound. AgentCatalog.opTool prints the new arguments into the MCP tools automatically. Favourite ranges are media-level ranges in source ticks, like media.speech, and need a format bump. A source viewer is a Swift AVPlayer view, and skimming can reuse the thumbs/ cache plus AVAssetImageGenerator. Proxies: a half-size render into cache/ on the ReverseRenderer/ReverseResolution pattern. But app/CLAUDE.md says CompositionBuilder must 'not be given a preview-shaped argument', since it is shared by preview, export and render_frame. A playback-only proxy swap therefore needs a recorded decision, like the reversed asset's per-clip substitution, so export and render_frame never read a proxy. Confirmed: the 8-concurrent-video-track budget only warns (plan.rs warnings_for). The proxies half also runs against the owner's 'features before performance' order: the GitHub project 'Frame Job — Performance' (#1) exists.
verdicts.platform_apis: AVPlayer / AVPlayerView for the viewer; AVAssetImageGenerator for skim frames; AVAssetWriter with AVVideoCodecType.proRes422Proxy or HEVC for proxies; existing source_window.rs bounds in the core.
verdicts.market_refutation_attempt: Tried 'creators don't need it'. The creator-first tools that win (Descript, Screen Studio, CapCut) sell on transcript and recording workflows, not a source monitor, and a single-take talking head is placed whole and cut. Tried 'Apple Silicon makes proxies moot': hardware decode of 4K H.264/HEVC is strong, so proxies only matter for multi-stream 4K or codecs the media engine does not accelerate (possibly the owner's GH5 10-bit 4:2:2; unverified, search budget exhausted). So the proxy half does not survive without a measurement. Source ranges, skimming and In/Out do survive as table stakes. Every NLE a creator graduates to (Final Cut, Premiere, Resolve) has them. A vlog or B-roll workflow without them means placing a whole file and blading it every time. They are also the precondition for placing a search hit or a found moment (C13, C6) and for multicam at 3–4 angles (C4). Gap-closing, not a differentiator.
verdicts.corrections: (a) CompositionBuilder+SourceRange.swift is about a log media's full/video RANGE FLAG (spec §11 GR-22/GR-23), unrelated to source ranges. (b) Issue #112 is 'Decide whether a left-hand media browser with bins is now due' (icebox, spec), not proxies or performance. (c) Performance is not measured 'only at 1080p': #56 (graphics at 4K), #258 (4K headroom, closed) and manual-checks rows (e.g. GR-35 '4K playback stays smooth') exist. What is missing is a multi-stream 4K or multi-hour measurement. (d) Preview Quality Half/Quarter already lowers render size, but not decode cost. (e) Split it: source ranges, skimming, In/Out and favourites (M) now; proxies only after a measurement shows a shortfall, under a recorded decision on a playback-only builder input.

verdicts.closest_existing: Per-media caches in the package (thumbs/, peaks/, loudness/, sync/, speech/ on MediaCacheLane; transcripts/ and device-transcripts/) and get_transcript, which reads ONE clip's words. No Vision, SoundAnalysis, FoundationModels or Translation import exists: the only ML import is CoreML in SileroVAD.swift. No cross-media search tool.
verdicts.feasibility: The per-file analyses exist on macOS, confirmed from Apple doc JSON: Vision VNClassifyImageRequest (10.15, a fixed label taxonomy), VNRecognizeTextRequest (10.15, on-screen text, a real asset for screencasts), VNDetectFaceRectanglesRequest (10.13), VNGeneratePersonSegmentationRequest (12.0) and VNGenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest (10.15, image-to-image similarity, which can find shot changes since Vision has no shot-change request). SoundAnalysis SNClassifySoundRequest with SNClassifierIdentifier.version1 (macOS 12.0) covers ~300 classes including laughter, applause and typing; Speech SpeechTranscriber is 26.0. Free-text visual search ('the dog') beyond Vision's labels needs a bundled image-text embedding model. Apple's MobileCLIP Core ML weights are published under 'apple-ascl', and the redistribution terms of LICENSE_weights_data were not verified. The index fits the existing cache pattern (CacheStamp marker, MediaCacheLane, CacheLedger.publish) with Rust owning the index format. Placing a hit needs C10's source-range add_clip. Background analysis of every frame costs real time and disk on long media. No conflict with Rust decides or BYO-key.
verdicts.platform_apis: Vision (VNClassifyImageRequest, VNRecognizeTextRequest, VNDetectFaceRectanglesRequest, VNGenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest), SoundAnalysis (SNClassifySoundRequest + SNClassifierIdentifier.version1, macOS 12.0+), Speech SpeechTranscriber (macOS 26.0+), optional bundled CLIP-class Core ML model (licence unverified).
verdicts.market_refutation_attempt: Tried commoditisation: Final Cut Pro 12 (Jan 2026, Creator Studio) ships Visual and Transcript Search, Resolve 21 ships IntelliSearch (sources conflict on free vs Studio), and Premiere ships Media Intelligence with an on-device semantic index. So within a year it became a baseline NLE feature and is not distinctive. Tried 'creators distrust it': Larry Jordan's test of FCP 12 visual search found 30 clips for 'horses', 23 of them with no horse, and called both searches 'highly limited and unreliable'. Tried niche: media search pays off in large-library or documentary work, while the core talking-head and screencast creator has one long take plus some B-roll, already reachable by get_transcript and the timeline. The 'agents can query it' angle is narrow: Adobe has an official hosted creativity MCP server (GA April 2026 per a vendor page; Premiere coverage unverified), and an agent can already read a clip's words. The case fails as a standalone L-sized headline. Its slices (faces for reframe, Sound Analysis for moments, OCR for screencasts, a cross-media transcript search tool) are worth building inside the features that consume them.
verdicts.corrections: (a) Confirmed: there are no Vision, SoundAnalysis, FoundationModels or Translation imports; CoreML appears only in SileroVAD.swift. (b) Vision has no shot-change request: shot changes would come from feature-print distances or a histogram pass. (c) Vision's own visual search is fixed-taxonomy labels. Free-text search needs a bundled model (e.g. MobileCLIP under apple-ascl, licence unverified). (d) Resolve IntelliSearch being 'Studio only' is disputed: one later guide says it works in both editions. (e) 'No NLE exposes its index to an agent' is only weakly true: Adobe runs an official hosted MCP server (coverage of Premiere search unverified), and Resolve has a scripting API. (f) Cheap slice worth keeping elsewhere: a search_media tool over the cached transcripts (S), and Sound Analysis or face tracks built inside C6 or C9. (g) Web search budget ran out before more evidence on creator demand for footage search could be gathered.

verdicts.closest_existing: Export sheet Loudness choices −14 LUFS (streaming) and −16 LUFS (podcast) with an always-on −1 dBTP master limiter; canvas presets Vertical 1080×1920 and Square; user-saved export presets (ExportPresetsStore.swift, ~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/ExportPresets.json); chapter markers embedded in MP4/MOV/M4A/WebM (ExporterWriter+Chapters.swift); View ▸ Safe Areas at 90%/80%; File ▸ Save Frame… (PNG/JPEG/HEIC); bundled 'Social & YouTube' graphic templates (End screen, Subscribe button, Handle tag, Social popup).
verdicts.feasibility: The deterministic half is easy. A copyable chapter list is a read of add_marker {chapter} markers, the same source ExporterWriter+Chapters.swift writes. A YouTube rule check (00:00 first, at least 3, each at least 10 s) is pure and could be a core validator. Platform targets can be built-in rows beside the user presets (ExportPresetsStore). Safe-zone overlays extend the existing guide drawing. The AI half is weak. FoundationModels SystemLanguageModel is macOS 26.0+ (Apple doc JSON) and is unavailable when appleIntelligenceNotEnabled, deviceNotEligible or modelNotReady. Its context is ~4,096 tokens shared by input and output (third-party sources, plus Apple's contextSize property), so a 20-minute talk's transcript (~3,000 words) does not fit in one session and must be chunked and summarised. Vision CalculateImageAestheticsScoresRequest is macOS 15.0+ (Apple doc JSON). No conflict with Rust decides or BYO-key, but an HLG project exported for Spotify needs the SDR version (Spotify down-converts Rec.2020).

verdicts.market_refutation_attempt: Tried commoditisation, and the distinctive half fails. YouTube Studio now offers AI title suggestions ('Ask Studio'), tests up to three titles AND thumbnails per video, suggests three frames for Shorts thumbnails and generates AI thumbnail concepts (TechCrunch, 2026-09-23). Tried 'rule checks prevent broken uploads': platforms re-encode almost anything. Demand for overlays exists, shown by many safe-zone checker tools, but it is polish. verdicts.closest_existing: Media tab rows with thumbnails, dragged whole onto a track (plain drop, ⌥ insert, ⇧⌥ overwrite), then trimmed or slipped on the timeline; View ▸ Preview Quality Full/Half/Quarter (render size only, not decode). No skimming (MediaRowView hover only paints a fill), no source viewer, no In/Out or favourite ranges on media, no proxies. add_clip, insert_clip and overwrite_clip take only track, media and at.
verdicts.feasibility: Source ranges are an op-table change: add_clip, insert_clip and overwrite_clip gain an optional source in and duration, held inside the file by source_window.rs's one bound. AgentCatalog.opTool prints the new arguments into the MCP tools automatically. Favourite ranges are media-level ranges in source ticks, like media.speech, and need a format bump. A source viewer is a Swift AVPlayer view, and skimming can reuse the thumbs/ cache plus AVAssetImageGenerator. Proxies: a half-size render into cache/ on the ReverseRenderer/ReverseResolution pattern. But app/CLAUDE.md says CompositionBuilder must 'not be given a preview-shaped argument', since it is shared by preview, export and render_frame. A playback-only proxy swap therefore needs a recorded decision, like the reversed asset's per-clip substitution, so export and render_frame never read a proxy. Confirmed: the 8-concurrent-video-track budget only warns (plan.rs warnings_for). The proxies half also runs against the owner's 'features before performance' order: the GitHub project 'Frame Job — Performance' (#1) exists.
verdicts.platform_apis: AVPlayer / AVPlayerView for the viewer; AVAssetImageGenerator for skim frames; AVAssetWriter with AVVideoCodecType.proRes422Proxy or HEVC for proxies; existing source_window.rs bounds in the core.
verdicts.market_refutation_attempt: Tried 'creators don't need it'. So the proxy half does not survive without a measurement. Source ranges, skimming and In/Out do survive as table stakes. Every NLE a creator graduates to (Final Cut, Premiere, Resolve) has them. A vlog or B-roll workflow without them means placing a whole file and blading it every time. verdicts.corrections: (a) CompositionBuilder+SourceRange.swift is about a log media's full/video RANGE FLAG (spec §11 GR-22/GR-23), unrelated to source ranges. (c) Performance is not measured 'only at 1080p': #56 (graphics at 4K), #258 (4K headroom, closed) and manual-checks rows (e.g. GR-35 '4K playback stays smooth') exist. What is missing is a multi-stream 4K or multi-hour measurement. (d) Preview Quality Half/Quarter already lowers render size, but not decode cost. (e) Split it: source ranges, skimming, In/Out and favourites (M) now; proxies only after a measurement shows a shortfall, under a recorded decision on a playback-only builder input.

verdicts.closest_existing: Per-media caches in the package (thumbs/, peaks/, loudness/, sync/, speech/ on MediaCacheLane; transcripts/ and device-transcripts/) and get_transcript, which reads ONE clip's words. Free-text visual search ('the dog') beyond Vision's labels needs a bundled image-text embedding model. Apple's MobileCLIP Core ML weights are published under 'apple-ascl', and the redistribution terms of LICENSE_weights_data were not verified. The index fits the existing cache pattern (CacheStamp marker, MediaCacheLane, CacheLedger.publish) with Rust owning the index format. Placing a hit needs C10's source-range add_clip. verdicts.market_refutation_attempt: Tried commoditisation: Final Cut Pro 12 (Jan 2026, Creator Studio) ships Visual and Transcript Search, Resolve 21 ships IntelliSearch (sources conflict on free vs Studio), and Premiere ships Media Intelligence with an on-device semantic index. So within a year it became a baseline NLE feature and is not distinctive. Tried 'creators distrust it': Larry Jordan's test of FCP 12 visual search found 30 clips for 'horses', 23 of them with no horse, and called both searches 'highly limited and unreliable'. Tried niche: media search pays off in large-library or documentary work, while the core talking-head and screencast creator has one long take plus some B-roll, already reachable by get_transcript and the timeline. The 'agents can query it' angle is narrow: Adobe has an official hosted creativity MCP server (GA April 2026 per a vendor page; Premiere coverage unverified), and an agent can already read a clip's words. verdicts.corrections: (a) Confirmed: there are no Vision, SoundAnalysis, FoundationModels or Translation imports; CoreML appears only in SileroVAD.swift. (d) Resolve IntelliSearch being 'Studio only' is disputed: one later guide says it works in both editions. (e) 'No NLE exposes its index to an agent' is only weakly true: Adobe runs an official hosted MCP server (coverage of Premiere search unverified), and Resolve has a scripting API. (f) Cheap slice worth keeping elsewhere: a search_media tool over the cached transcripts (S), and Sound Analysis or face tracks built inside C6 or C9. (g) Web search budget ran out before more evidence on creator demand for footage search could be gathered.

verdicts.closest_existing: Clip ▸ Remove Silences… and Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words… (sheet, timeline wash, one ripple_delete_ranges undo step; detect_silence/detect_fillers MCP tools), plus get_transcript + ripple_delete_ranges driven by the Assistant for false starts (TR-5). verdicts.feasibility: Feasible, and it reuses existing parts. Word timings are cached per media in MEDIA source ticks (DeviceTranscriptCache.swift: cache/device-transcripts/<media>-<lang>.json; AssemblyAI in cache/transcripts/). MediaTranscript.words(for:in:) and TranscriptReader map them onto a clip in project ticks. rc_project_source_map (ffi_query.rs:146, SR-20) maps through speed, ramps and reverse. ripple_delete_ranges (op_table.rs:273) merges many ranges into ONE undo step and is an MCP tool. FillerDetector already holds the lock, nest and transition protection rules, so a text cut can reuse them. Gaps: (1) Restore is not one existing op. add_clip, insert_clip and overwrite_clip take only track, media and at, so restoring a cut word means insert_time + trim_end into the left clip's handle as one grouped step, and insert_time also shifts every other unlocked track. (2) A whole-timeline view needs the on-device recogniser over every clip, at 'a few seconds per minute of speech', before it fills. Cached per media after that. (3) Fillers in the view are cloud-only: TR-7 measured that the on-device engine kept 1 of 8 fillers. Without an AssemblyAI key the view shows no fillers. (4) MAX_CLIPS = 4096 counts nested clips too (format.rs check_caps). Each text cut splits EVERY unlocked track, so about 1,000 cuts over a 4-track timeline reaches the cap. CONFLICT with spec §11: TR-3 says 'a false start is never offered without a conversation', and AI-6/W-9 say 'no PIPELINE picks words to cut by meaning'. A deterministic retake/false-start pass that strikes words for review is such a pipeline, so it needs a new §11 decision amending TR-3 before code. Fillers and long pauses are fine under TR-3/TR-4. No format change is needed, because cut words are derivable as media words lying between consecutive windows of the same media.
verdicts.platform_apis: Speech SpeechTranscriber (macOS 26.0+, Apple doc JSON) for the on-device transcript; AssemblyAI (BYO key, existing) for fillers and speaker labels; AVPlayer periodic time observer for the word highlight. No new framework needed.
verdicts.market_refutation_attempt: Tried commoditisation: edit-by-transcript is everywhere. Descript, CapCut desktop and Riverside delete-word editing; Screen Studio 4.0 (Oct 2026: delete sentences, filler and pause removal); Premiere's Text-Based Editing plus Paper Edit in 26.5 (Sept 2026); Gling (silences, fillers, bad takes). So it is NOT distinctive. Tried 'creators distrust it': Gling reviewers say its bad-take detection 'will cut takes you wanted', and Screen Studio users complain about Whisper accuracy. Cap's transcript editor is only an open PR dated June 2026, merge unconfirmed, and no 2026 evidence was found for Tella Auto Cut or Loom transcript trim. verdicts.corrections: (a) Cap: transcript editing is an open PR (June 2026), not confirmed shipped. Tella Auto Cut and Loom transcript trim are unverified in 2026. (c) The retake/false-start pass conflicts with spec §11 TR-3 (and AI-6/W-9) and needs an amending §11 decision first. (d) Restoring a cut is not an existing op: it is insert_time + trim_end, or add_clip gaining a source range (C10). (e) Fillers 'found for you' require an AssemblyAI key (TR-7); on-device, the view shows no fillers. (f) Effort is a road map (view and seek; delete as ranges; greyed restorable words; retakes after a §11 decision), not M.

verdicts.closest_existing: Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio (move_clip + drift-correcting set_speed as one undo step); per-media Silero speech spans (media_speech.rs, format 29) read per clip by Duck by Speech (audio_duck_speech.rs); the Channels section (AU-34: left/right/both/swapped of a two-channel track); set_enabled. verdicts.feasibility: Feasible as a planner over cached data. So OBS multi-track files lose tracks 2+. Fixing this means an audio-track index on the media or clip (format bump) and touches every firstTrack(.audio) caller, not just the builder. Confirmed: the 8-decoder budget only WARNS (plan.rs warnings_for). Helpful finding: a clip with enabled.video off is NOT decoded, because nest.rs shows_video gates evaluate.rs:454/477 and the recipe. So stacked angles disabled by set_enabled cost one decode at a time, except in transition overlaps. One undo step does NOT need a new core op: Synchronize Audio already applies an op list as one step. A core op (split + set_enabled across tracks) is wanted for MCP parity and because a 2-hour episode emits thousands of ops. Clip cap: 2 h at one cut per ~8 s is ~900 cuts. Splitting all 3 angle tracks gives ~2,700 clips. If each angle carries a linked sound half (AU-90) that is split with it, ~5,400 is OVER MAX_CLIPS 4096. So the design must cut picture only, keep the mics whole, or use a single program track. Spec §1 lists multicam as a deliberate non-goal (confirmed), so a §11 decision lifting it is needed first. Inputs exist: Silero spans per media through Core ML (SileroVAD.swift), the 10 ms loudness cache, Match Audio and Enhance Voice. AssemblyAI speaker labels exist for captions (BYO key) as an optional diarisation source.

SoundAnalysis SNClassifySoundRequest with SNClassifierIdentifier.version1 (macOS 12.0) covers ~300 classes including laughter, applause and typing; Speech SpeechTranscriber is 26.0. Free-text visual search ('the dog') beyond Vision's labels needs a bundled image-text embedding model. Apple's MobileCLIP Core ML weights are published under 'apple-ascl', and the redistribution terms of LICENSE_weights_data were not verified. The index fits the existing cache pattern (CacheStamp marker, MediaCacheLane, CacheLedger.publish) with Rust owning the index format. Placing a hit needs C10's source-range add_clip. Background analysis of every frame costs real time and disk on long media. No conflict with Rust decides or BYO-key.
verdicts.platform_apis: Vision (VNClassifyImageRequest, VNRecognizeTextRequest, VNDetectFaceRectanglesRequest, VNGenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest), SoundAnalysis (SNClassifySoundRequest + SNClassifierIdentifier.version1, macOS 12.0+), Speech SpeechTranscriber (macOS 26.0+), optional bundled CLIP-class Core ML model (licence unverified).
verdicts.market_refutation_attempt: Tried commoditisation: Final Cut Pro 12 (Jan 2026, Creator Studio) ships Visual and Transcript Search, Resolve 21 ships IntelliSearch (sources conflict on free vs Studio), and Premiere ships Media Intelligence with an on-device semantic index. So within a year it became a baseline NLE feature and is not distinctive. Tried 'creators distrust it': Larry Jordan's test of FCP 12 visual search found 30 clips for 'horses', 23 of them with no horse, and called both searches 'highly limited and unreliable'. Tried niche: media search pays off in large-library or documentary work, while the core talking-head and screencast creator has one long take plus some B-roll, already reachable by get_transcript and the timeline. The 'agents can query it' angle is narrow: Adobe has an official hosted creativity MCP server (GA April 2026 per a vendor page; Premiere coverage unverified), and an agent can already read a clip's words. The case fails as a standalone L-sized headline. Its slices (faces for reframe, Sound Analysis for moments, OCR for screencasts, a cross-media transcript search tool) are worth building inside the features that consume them.
verdicts.corrections: (a) Confirmed: there are no Vision, SoundAnalysis, FoundationModels or Translation imports; CoreML appears only in SileroVAD.swift. (b) Vision has no shot-change request: shot changes would come from feature-print distances or a histogram pass. (c) Vision's own visual search is fixed-taxonomy labels. Free-text search needs a bundled model (e.g. MobileCLIP under apple-ascl, licence unverified). (d) Resolve IntelliSearch being 'Studio only' is disputed: one later guide says it works in both editions. (e) 'No NLE exposes its index to an agent' is only weakly true: Adobe runs an official hosted MCP server (coverage of Premiere search unverified), and Resolve has a scripting API. (f) Cheap slice worth keeping elsewhere: a search_media tool over the cached transcripts (S), and Sound Analysis or face tracks built inside C6 or C9. (g) Web search budget ran out before more evidence on creator demand for footage search could be gathered.
